simple.meaning: אֵצֶל (ʼêtsel) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a side ; (as a preposition) near.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 61 times in Genesis, Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 10 more, beginning at Genesis 39:10. The surrounding contexts include altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵצֶל (H681) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֵצֶל (ʼêtsel) / H681 is traced through Genesis 39:10, Genesis 39:15, Genesis 39:16, Genesis 39:18 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.usage: at, (hard) by, (from) (beside), near (unto), toward, with. See also 1018 .
definitions.full: H681. etsel I. אֵ֫צֶל 61 substantive conjunction, proximity ; with suffix אֶצְלוֺ אֶצְלִי, etc.; only used as a preposition a. (as an implicit accusative) in proximity to (as though Lag BN 68 ), beside: Gen 39:10 , 15 ; 41:3 and stood הַמַּרוֺת אֵצֶל beside the kine, 1Sam 5:2 דָּגוֺן אֵצֶל beside Dagon, 1Kin 13:24-25 , 21:1 ; Prov 8:30 ; Ezek 1:15 , 19 ; 33:30 ; 39:15 ; often in phrase ( ׳מ ׳י ) הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אֵצֶל Lev 1:16 ; 6:3 ; Deut 16:21 ; 1Kin 2:29 ; Amos 2:8 +; of a locality (compare II. אֵת 2 ) Deut 11:30 beside the terebinths of Moreh, 1Kin 1:9 ; 4:12 ; Jer 41:17 . After a verb of motion (late) Dan 8:7 , 17 ; compare 2Chr 28:15 b. b. with מֵאֵצֶל מִן, from proximity to, from beside (compare מֵעִם מֵאֵת, ): 1Sam 20:41 (read with הָאַרְגָּב מֵאֵצֶל ᵐ5 from beside the mound); Ezek 40:7 contiguous to, beside ( מִן 3c ); with suffix 1Sam 17:30 מֵאֶצְלוֺ וַיָּסָב and he turned about from beside him , 1Kin 3:20 ; 20:36 ; Ezek 10:16 .
